# Ensure every Main Street card has dedicated card art (1024×1024 source)

## Problem statement

Every Main Street card renders a square art zone in its top-left corner, but
**108 of the 171 unique cards in `card-data.csv` currently render the same
generic `Fallback` sprite**, so the bulk of the deck is visually
indistinguishable. A player cannot tell an `Upgrade to Patisserie` from a
`Chef` from a `Rainy Day` at a glance, which undermines the 64×64 left-art
redesign's whole purpose.

## Users

- **Player (market / hand / street):** needs to recognise a card by its art
  without reading the title — especially when cards overlap in hand or stack
  on the street.
- **Content author:** needs a documented, testable rule for what art a card
  resolves to, so new cards cannot silently reintroduce `Fallback` art.
- **Engine maintainer:** needs one art-resolution path shared by the runtime
  generator and the static SVG exporter, guarded by a regression test.

User stories:

- As a player, when I look at the market, I can tell any two cards apart by
  their art alone.
- As an upgrade card, I show the art of the business I enhance under my new
  display name, so my purpose is obvious.
- As a content author, when I add a card to `card-data.csv`, the test suite
  tells me if I forgot to give it art.

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-26)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q1 | Art scope / strategy | **Option A — reuse-first.** Actively **duplicate the existing art under the new (card/display) name**, and produce **new art only where necessary** (no suitable existing art). |
| Q2 | Art production ownership | **The producer will produce the new sprites.** This item still owns the mapping, resolver, regeneration tooling and the drift guard. |
| Q3 | Event mapping granularity | **Map events by `trigger` × `targetSynergy` category** (a documented, generated mapping). |

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-29)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q4 | Source-art size | The producer provides **1024×1024** source art (`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`). The “64×64” is the on-card display zone, not the production size. |
| Q5 | Staff art granularity | **One sprite per staff role** (24 sprites). |
| Q6 | Event-category art | **Unique (bespoke) sprite per `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category** — representatives are not reused. |
| Q7 | Drift-guard tightening | **Yes** — tighten the guard to a strict “zero `Fallback` for every card in `card-data.csv`” assertion once the sprites land, in the same change. |
| Q8 | Duplicate-name clash | **Rename to remove the clashes**: business `Florist` → `Flower Shop`; event `Community Garden` → `Garden Party`. |

Art-production ownership (Q2, 2026-09-26) is unchanged: the producer supplies
all new source sprites.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-26, `dev` @ 933644bc)

Resolution path (all four card families call it with the card's `name`):

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` → `resolveCardArtName()` /
  `hasDedicatedCardArt()`: (1) spelling alias → (2) exact name → (3)
  `Fallback`.
- Map built by `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs`
  from committed `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` files into
  `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json`.
- A second consumer, `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`,
  duplicates the alias/lookup logic and must be kept in step.

Verified counts:

- `card-data.csv`: **173 rows / 171 unique names** (duplicate names across
  families: `Florist` = business + staff, `Community Garden` = community-space
  + event → name-keyed resolution shares one sprite).
- Committed sprites: **62 dedicated + `Fallback`** (63 map entries).
- Cards resolving today: **65** (63 exact + 2 via aliases).
- **Cards rendering `Fallback`: 108**:

| Family              | Cards | Resolving | Missing |
|---------------------|------:|----------:|--------:|
| business            |    30 |        28 |       2 |
| community-space     |     8 |         1 |       7 |
| upgrade             |    39 |         0 |      39 |
| staff               |    25 |         1 |      24 |
| event               |    71 |        35 |      36 |
| **Total**           |  **173** | **65** | **108** |

Every missing card already has an `art_notes` description in `card-data.csv`
(the source the existing 1024×1024 sprites were built from). There is **no
in-repo image generator** — the existing sprites were committed out-of-band
(commit `05026750`), and the producer will continue producing new art the same
way.

## Size clarification (reviewed 2026-09-29)

The “64×64” in the original title is the **on-card display zone** — a layout
dimension in SVG user units — **not** the size of the source art to produce.
Code review of the generator and renderer confirms three distinct layers:

| Layer | Size | Where | Role |
|-------|-----:|-------|------|
| On-card art zone | 64×64 | `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` (`GRAPHIC_*`) | SVG layout box only |
| Embedded bitmap | 256×256 | `src/card-art-map.json` (`artResolution`) | WebP `data:` URI in the SVG |
| **Source art** | **1024×1024** | `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` | Generator input |

`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` only loads files named
`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` (`SOURCE_SUFFIX = '_1024_x_1024.png'`) and downscales
each to 256×256 WebP (`ART_RESOLUTION = 256`). Phaser rasterises the card SVG
at `qualityScale = max(4, dpr)`, so the 64×64 zone needs a ≥256×256 bitmap to
stay crisp; a 64×64 source would be stretched ~4× and appear pixelated.

**Produce every new sprite at 1024×1024**, named `<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`, in
`src/sprites/`. The legacy `<Name>_64_x_64.png` files are superseded
thumbnails and are not read by the generator.

## Progress (2026-09-29)

The mapping/resolver/tooling + pending-aware drift guard landed on `dev` as
commit `4b80741` (full unit suite green): `src/card-art-map.json` is now
`version: 3`. Real coverage rose from **65 → 95 of 171** unique cards.

**Duplicate names split (commit `874f419`).** On producer decision Q8 the two
duplicate card names were renamed, so all **173 card names are now unique**:

- business `Florist` → **`Flower Shop`** — keeps the existing rose sprite
  (renamed `Flower Shop_1024_x_1024.png`); its `upgradePath` and
  `Upgrade to Garden Center`'s `targetBusiness` both follow.
- event `Community Garden` → **`Garden Party`** — now needs its own art and maps
  to the `Investment__` category until then.
- staff `Florist` keeps its name; its business restriction is now
  `Flower Shop|Commerce|Culture`.

Card IDs are intentionally unchanged (`biz-florist`, `evt-community-garden`) to
preserve save/challenge compatibility. After the split, **95 of 173** cards
resolve and **78** still render `Fallback`: the staff `Florist` and event
`Garden Party` joined the pending set, giving **46 distinct source sprites** to
produce.

## Desired change (confirmed strategy)

1. **Upgrades (39) — duplicate target art under the new display name.**
   For each `Upgrade to …`, copy the art of its `targetBusiness` to a new
   source sprite named after the upgrade's `newDisplayName` (all 39 are
   distinct, no collisions, and none is already a sprite). Seven targets are
   themselves gaps, so their art must be produced first: `Cafe`,
   `Health Kiosk`, `Laundromat`, `Library`, `Park`, `Playground`,
   `Town Fountain`.
2. **Business / community-space gaps (9) — new art.** `Laundromat`, `Cafe` and
   all community spaces except `Community Garden`: `Park`, `Library`,
   `Playground`, `Town Fountain`, `Health Kiosk`, `Community Shelter`,
   `Public Art`.
3. **Staff (25) — new staff art.** **One sprite per staff role** (confirmed
   2026-09-29), produced by the producer. The split moved `Florist` (staff)
   off the shared business sprite, so all 25 roles need art.
4. **Events (37) — category mapping.** Map each event to a category sprite
   keyed by `(trigger, targetSynergy)`; **unique (bespoke) art per category**
   (confirmed 2026-09-29), produced by the producer. `Garden Party` joined the
   category-mapped set after the split.
5. **Resolver / map.** Extend the generated mapping (and/or `CARD_ART_ALIASES`)
   so both consumers agree and regeneration stays deterministic; keep
   `Fallback` only as the genuine last resort.
6. **Drift guard.** Add a unit test over `card-data.csv` asserting full
   coverage and failing when a new art-less card appears.

## Required art (derived)

| Group | Cards | Mechanism | New sprites |
|-------|------:|-----------|------------:|
| Upgrade | 39 | Duplicate `targetBusiness` art under each upgrade's `newDisplayName` | 0 new (39 copies) |
| Business + community-space gaps | 9 | New source art | 9 |
| Staff | 25 | New source art — one per role | 25 |
| Event | 37 | Unique `(trigger × targetSynergy)` category art — 12 categories | 12 |
| **Total distinct source sprites** | | | **46** |

Event categories for the 36 missing events (representative = an event with
dedicated art today in the same category, available to duplicate):

| `trigger` | `targetSynergy` | Cards | Existing representative |
|-----------|-----------------|------:|-------------------------|
| Incident  | (none)          | 9 | Tax Audit |
| Incident  | Culture         | 1 | Cultural Grant |
| Incident  | Entertainment   | 1 | Noise Complaint |
| Incident  | Food            | 6 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Health          | 1 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Service         | 4 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| (none)          | 3 | Charity Drive |
| Investment| Commerce        | 1 | Grand Opening Sale |
| Investment| Entertainment   | 3 | Street Performer |
| Investment| Food            | 2 | Harvest Festival |
| Investment| Health          | 3 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| Service         | 2 | *(none — new)* |

Existing dedicated event art (35 events) is retained; only the 36 missing
events are category-mapped. **The producer confirmed on 2026-09-29 that each of
the 12 categories gets unique (bespoke) art** — the “existing representative”
column above is informational only and is not reused.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every **unique** card name in `card-data.csv` resolves via
   `MainStreetCardArt.hasDedicatedCardArt()` to a **non-`Fallback`** sprite
   (documented alias/category mapping counts); currently 65/171.
2. All 39 upgrade cards resolve to art duplicated from their `targetBusiness`
   under the upgrade's `newDisplayName`; no upgrade renders `Fallback`.
3. All 24 staff cards resolve to dedicated staff art; no staff card renders
   `Fallback`.
4. All 36 missing event cards resolve to a documented
   `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category sprite; no event card renders `Fallback`.
5. All 9 business / community-space gaps resolve to dedicated art; no card in
   either family renders `Fallback`.
6. A unit-test drift guard over `card-data.csv` asserts AC 1–5 and fails when a
   new card is added without art; `Fallback` remains in the map and resolver for
   genuinely-unknown/future cards (the existing "unknown card" test still passes).
7. Both consumers of `card-art-map.json` (runtime `MainStreetCardArt.ts` and
   `scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) apply the identical mapping;
   regeneration via `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` is
   deterministic and reproducible.
8. `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` and `public/assets/CREDITS.md`
   document the mapping rules and the licence/attribution of any new art.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
10. `npm run build` is green and the **full project test suite must pass** with
    the new changes.

## Constraints

- New art must be permissively licensed (CC0 / MIT / Apache 2.0) and attributed
  in `public/assets/CREDITS.md`.
- Source art remains `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`; `card-art-map.json`
  stays generated (never hand-edited).
- No change to the 64×64 zone geometry, the 140×80 card size, the 256×256
  embedded WebP format, or the SVG being self-contained (inline `data:` URI).
- Mapping logic must be expressed once and consumed by both the runtime and the
  static generator.

## Desired artefacts

- Up to 45 new `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` source files (9 business /
  community-space, 24 staff, up to 12 event categories) and 39 upgrade
  duplicates named by `newDisplayName`.
- Updated generated mapping + resolver.
- Drift-guard unit test in `tests/main-street/`.
- Docs + credits updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` — resolver: targetBusiness /
  category resolution or extended alias path.
- `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` — regenerated mapping (data).
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` —
  derive the upgrade-duplication and event-category mapping from
  `card-data.csv` + sprites.
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` —
  second consumer; mirror the mapping.
- `example-games/main-street/sprites/` — new + duplicated `_1024_x_1024.png`
  source art (producer).
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — add the `card-data.csv` drift guard.
- `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — document mapping rules.
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md` — licence/attribution for new art.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Art-availability dependency:** the resolver/tooling can land independently,
  but AC 1–5 cannot pass until the producer's sprites are committed. Plan
  should sequence tooling + drift guard first, art last.
- **Duplicate-name collision (resolved 2026-09-29):** the business `Florist`
  and the event `Community Garden` were renamed to `Flower Shop` and
  `Garden Party` (Q8), so every card name is now unique and no sprite is shared
  across families. IDs are unchanged for save/challenge compatibility.
- **Category-art fidelity (resolved 2026-09-29):** the producer confirmed
  unique (bespoke) art for all 12 event categories, so no representative
  sprite is reused.
- **Dual-consumer drift risk:** `generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` duplicates
  the alias logic; a mapping change that misses it silently diverges — assert
  both in tests.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "improve the existing 62 sprites" and "redesign the art
  zone" are out of scope — record separately if they surface.
- **Assumption:** `hasDedicatedCardArt()` remains name-keyed; any targetBusiness
  indirection is baked into the generated map so the public API is unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Changing the 64×64 left-art geometry or the 140×80 card dimensions.
- New card types or `card-data.csv` content changes (beyond `art_notes` if new
  art needs them).
- Filling the empty gameplay `description` column on the 45 `event` rows
  (unrelated to art; all 173 rows already carry `art_notes`).
- Redesigning/replacing the existing 62 dedicated sprites.
- Adding an in-repo image-generation tool (the producer supplies the art).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 "Art scope / strategy: how much new art vs. mapping/reuse for the 108
  cards?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):** Option A — actively duplicate
  the current art using the new name; new art where necessary. Source:
  interactive producer reply.
- Q2 "Art production ownership & pipeline: who produces the new sprites, and
  does this item ship mapping machinery first?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-26):** "I will produce them." Source: interactive producer reply.
  Research: no in-repo sprite generator exists (last sprite commit
  `05026750`, external).
- Q3 "Event mapping granularity: what taxonomy, and is a category sprite
  acceptable for AC4?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):**
  `trigger` × `targetSynergy` categories. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q1 prior/open record superseded by the answers above (was OPEN QUESTION).
- Q4 "Source-art size: 64×64 or 1024×1024?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** the producer provides **1024×1024** source art; the 64×64 is
  the on-card display zone. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q5 "Staff art granularity: per-role or shared?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** **one sprite per role**. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q6 "Event-category art: reuse a representative or unique?" — **Answer
  (producer, 2026-09-29):** **unique** per category. Source: interactive
  producer reply.
- Q7 "Tighten the drift guard to strict zero-`Fallback` once art lands?" —
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-29):** **yes**. Source: interactive producer
  reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MP1QZC6Q005EMEZ** – Asset generation: placeholder SVGs for new cards (completed)
- **CG-0MLTFDAYD0J6KLY3** – Phaser Scene Static Card Layout (completed)
- **CG-0MPD5XALT007F1WV** – Gym Graphics: Card Flip Animation (DeckRng + HandPile) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 0mtorj5fs006b0un, acceptance, add, alias, apache (+136 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — matched: acceptance, add, approach, art, asserts (+107 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, add, alias, apache, approach (+104 more)

# Action classification for Summary tab

Add an optional `action` property to the `LogEntry` type and set it at every player- and AI-initiated action `addLog` call site. Turn headers and the per-turn monetary summary rows deliberately leave it unset, so the Summary tab can structurally distinguish action rows from summary rows.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Action classification is structural, not textual: the turn record exposes an explicit action marker (an optional category on `LogEntry`, set wherever a player- or AI-initiated action is logged), so no rendered action row depends on matching log message text.
- `LogEntry` in `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` carries an optional `action` field (a string categorising the action type).
- Every `addLog` call site that records a player- or AI-initiated action (placing a business, hiring staff, playing an upgrade/event, moving a card to hand, selling, laying off, closing a street card, loans, challenge completions) sets the `action` field to a consistent category string.
- Turn headers and per-turn monetary summary rows (income/reputation lines) carry no `action` marker.
- A guard test asserts that every known action-producing `addLog` call site sets the marker, catching regressions.
- All existing tests pass.

**Key Files:**
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — add optional `action` to `LogEntry`
- `src/MainStreetStateLog.ts` and all `addLog` call sites — set the marker at action sites
- `tests/main-street/log-entry-action-marker.test.ts` — guard test

## Minimal Implementation
- Add optional `action?: string` to the `LogEntry` interface.
- Enumerate action category constants for each action type.
- Set the `action` field at each `addLog` call site that records a player- or AI-initiated action.
- Leave turn headers and monetary summary rows unset.

## Deliverables
- Updated `LogEntry` type, marked call sites, guard test.

## Dependencies
None — this is a foundational, additive change.

# Integrate Summary tab into Turn Summary overlay

Insert the `[ Summary ]` tab into the Turn Summary overlay, mark it as default, render its body sections, and attach per-figure tooltip zones within the existing panel geometry.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Turn Summary overlay presents a `[ Summary ]` tab as its **first** tab and selects it by default, in both single-player and competitive closings, leaving the existing per-player tabs (`You` / `AI n`) unchanged and still selectable.
- The Summary tab's sections render in the confirmed order **Major actions → Events → Income/Reputation/Score**.
- The Summary tab participates in tab navigation: pointer selection, Left/Right keyboard cycling and the selected-tab preservation after a mid-game loan take all include it, and selection is signalled with the panel's existing bold-selected convention.
- Every seat's figure on the Summary tab carries a hover/tap tooltip via `attachHudTooltipZone` using the Summary-row content builders.
- Presentation-only and absent-safe: no state mutation, no RNG consumption, no new persisted field; a result carrying no ledger of either shape still advances the closing immediately instead of stranding it; reduced-motion, replay and headless pacing are unchanged.
- Panel geometry is respected: the summary layout stays within the fixed 680×640 panel for a full competitive roster (bounded row counts where needed).
- All existing tests pass.

**Key Files:**
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryOverlay.ts` — insert `[ Summary ]` tab, mark default, render body, attach tooltips
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-pl-overlay.browser.test.ts` — extend for Summary tab tab-strip parity

## Minimal Implementation
- Insert a `Summary` tab in the tab strip before `You` and mark it default.
- Render the model's sections in the tab body using the existing panel typography.
- Attach `attachHudTooltipZone` to each figure.
- Wire tab navigation (pointer, keyboard, post-loan-take preservation).

## Deliverables
- Updated overlay, tab strip, rendering, tooltip zones, browser tab-strip parity tests.

## Dependencies
- MS-0MWBYWAZ80099DZT: Add LogEntry action marker and set at call sites
- MS-0MWBYZWYL008823N: Build Summary-tab model builder

# Per-card expense breakdowns on competitive Turn Summary seats

**discovered-from:MS-0MWBCACHZ006RTQ9**

## Problem statement

On a competitive closing, each seat's Turn Summary expense rows (Staff wages,
Community spaces, Business costs) are category totals only: the tooltip can
explain the committed figure but cannot list the individual cards, because
`CompetitiveRoundLedger` carries no per-card cost detail and
`buildCompetitiveTurnSummary` builds expense rows from
`buildExpenseRows(seat.ongoingCosts)`.

## Desired change

Derive each seat's per-card expense detail from the committed state
(owner-filtered `state.streetGrid` / `state.staffCards`) with the same
helpers single-player uses, thread it into the competitive P&L projection, and
render the same per-item multi-line breakdown every other tab now shows.

## Scope notes

- Deferred from MS-0MWBCACHZ006RTQ9 (A2): single-player and competitive income/
  incident/total/context detail is already at parity; this closes the remaining
  expense gap.
- Must remain absent-safe and deterministic; tests + docs required; full suite
  must pass.

**Headline:** A **Company Roster** overlay — opened by clicking the Staff Pile — lists every management-company staff member with role, salary and the exact cost of letting them go, and dismisses any one of them after a confirm step, closing the last gap where a hired staff member could not be let go from the UI.

## Problem statement

Management-company staff cannot be let go from any UI. The only lay-off path is the business Manage-Card dialog (`showSellConfirmation`, `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts:947`), which enumerates staff with `employedAtSlot === slotIndex` — a condition management-company staff never satisfy. The GDD (D.4.2 §5) assigns their lay-off to "the company roster", which does not exist. A player who hires a €500/turn Executive therefore pays its salary for the rest of the run with no way out.

## Users

- **Main Street player (hands-on)** — hired a management-company staff member, wants it gone, and cannot find any control that does it.
  - As a player, I want to see my management-company staff in one place and let one go, so that a bad hire is recoverable.
  - As a player, I want to see what letting someone go will cost *before* I commit, so that I can weigh the salary saving against the one-off hit.
- **Main Street player (economy-focused / learning the costs)** — plans the management team around salary load.
  - As a player, I want each member's per-turn salary and the roster's total alongside the lay-off price, so that I can decide whether cutting a role pays for itself.
- **Game designer / QA** — needs the roster to be an inspectable surface for the documented lay-off rule.
  - As QA, I want the roster's rows, totals and quoted lay-off cost to match the engine's own figures, so that a change to the salary or reputation rule cannot leave the UI quoting stale numbers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Clicking the Staff Pile — either the card-face stack or the portrait row beneath it — opens a **Company Roster** overlay; the existing hover tooltip still works, and hand-card clicks, hand→street drags and market→hand drops around the pile and the open dialog behave exactly as they do today.
- The roster lists every management-company staff member — `state.staffCards` filtered by `!isBusinessStaffCard(card)` — exactly once, in a stable order, each row showing the member's name, its role/benefit summary, and its effective per-turn salary (resolved through `computeStaffSalaryCost(getSalaryScopeSkills(member), member.ongoingCost)`, never a UI-invented figure); business staff never appear.
- The roster footer states the member count and the total per-turn salary of the management team, and both update immediately when a member is let go.
- Each row offers `[ Lay off ]`, which opens a confirm step quoting the member's name, one turn's salary (coins, clamped at 0) and the reputation cost; `[ Confirm ]` executes the existing `letGoStaffCommand` through the undo manager (so the lay-off stays undoable) and `[ Cancel ]` changes nothing.
- The lay-off reputation cost becomes `max(100, ceil(salary / 100) × 100)` — the GDD's flat "1 reputation" rescaled to the shipped ×100 reputation units (€50 salary → 100, €150 → 200, €250 → 300, €500 → 500); it is applied uniformly to **every** lay-off in `letGoStaffMember()` (management-company and business staff alike), with the coin and reputation deductions both clamped at 0.
- The roster reflects state without being reopened: after a lay-off the row disappears, the footer totals change and the Staff Pile's stack/count updates; when the last member leaves, the roster shows an explicit empty state ("No management-company staff employed.") rather than an empty panel, and is suppressed entirely in `replayMode`/headless runs like every other overlay.
- Unit tests cover the roster model — membership filtering, ordering, per-row salary, footer totals, and the reputation-cost formula at its boundaries (salary 0, 50, 100, 150, 250, 500) — and the existing lay-off expectations that assert a flat −1 reputation are updated; browser/render tests cover opening from the pile click, row content, confirm/cancel, post-lay-off refresh, the empty state, and that the pile's click does not swallow hand-card input.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A player can finally see their whole management team in one place and let a member go — with the salary saving and the reputation hit quoted up front — instead of paying a bad hire's salary for the rest of the run.

## Constraints

- **One engine rule, one UI surface.** The only engine change is the reputation formula in `letGoStaffMember()`; no new command, no new persisted state field. The roster is derived from `state.staffCards` on open and after each lay-off.
- **Reuse the existing command and overlay kit.** Lay-off goes through `letGoStaffCommand` (snapshot → undoable); the dialog is built from `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton` / `dismissOverlay`, following the `showStorylineJournalDialog` row-list precedent. No new overlay framework.
- **Two-type model stays authoritative.** Membership is `!isBusinessStaffCard(card)` — never a card-name list and never `employedAtSlot` re-derived inline.
- **The pile owns no roster logic.** The Staff Pile hands off a pointer-down (callback or scene method); all roster state, rows and lay-off wiring live in the roster module/overlay.
- **Quote engine figures, never re-derive them.** Salaries come from `computeStaffSalaryCost`/`getSalaryScopeSkills`; the lay-off coin cost and reputation cost come from the same helpers the command uses, so the confirm step cannot drift from what is actually charged.
- **No input hijack.** The pile's added click must not intercept hand-card clicks, drags or drops; assert it in the browser tests.
- **No new art.** Portraits/card faces reuse `mainStreetRenderCardSvg`.
- **Localisation.** New user-visible strings follow the `HUD_TOOLTIP_I18N_KEYS` / `HUD_TOOLTIP_STRINGS` English-bundle pattern introduced by the pile work where a key fits; overlay-only labels may follow the journal overlay's literal-string precedent.
- **Blocked by the Staff Pile.** The entry point is the pile (parent MS-0MWBWKZ1G006IBH2, amended); implementation starts only once the pile renders and hovers.
- **UK English**, no `CHANGELOG.md` edits (managed by the release pipeline).

## Existing state

- `state.staffCards` holds every hired member. `employedAtSlot` present ⇒ business staff; absent ⇒ management-company staff. `isBusinessStaffCard()` (`src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts`) is the canonical type test.
- `letGoStaffMember()` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:1513`) already removes the member, charges one turn's salary clamped at 0, charges a flat **1** reputation clamped at 0, and deregisters it from a business's `employedStaff` (a no-op for slotless members). `letGoStaffCommand()` (`src/MainStreetCommands.ts:903`) wraps it in a snapshot for undo.
- The Manage-Card dialog (`src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts:683-975`) is the only lay-off UI: it lists `employedAtSlot === slotIndex` and always acts on `employedStaff[employedStaff.length - 1]`. No management-company member ever appears.
- The Staff Pile (parent MS-0MWBWKZ1G006IBH2) is mid-implementation: layout zone, renderer module and tooltip builder are planned children, not yet shipped. Its tooltip is management-company-only; its ACs now permit exactly one click affordance (opening this roster).
- Overlay precedent: `showStorylineJournalDialog()` (`src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts:1655`) builds a 560-wide panel, title, row list capped at 10, "…and N earlier" overflow line, empty state, and `[ Close ]`; `s.replayMode` short-circuits before any drawing.
- Currency scale: reputation ships in ×100 units (starting reputation 200/300/500 by difficulty; discarding a card deducts its coin `cost` in reputation). The GDD's pre-scale "1 reputation" therefore reads as 100 today — this item records that rescale explicitly rather than leaving two scales in the docs.
- Tests that assert the current flat −1: `tests/main-street/manage-card-dialog.browser.test.ts` ("1 salary + 1 reputation" — sets reputation 5, expects 4), plus lay-off calls in `tests/main-street/staff-skill-scope-gate.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/MainStreetIntegration.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/staff-placement-removal.browser.test.ts`.
- Docs stating the flat −1: `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` (D.4.2 §5) and `docs/game/card-catalog.md:620`.

## Desired change

1. **Engine (one rule).** In `letGoStaffMember()`, replace the flat −1 with `max(100, ceil(salary / 100) × 100)` where `salary` is the already-computed effective salary, clamped at 0 as today. Comment the ×100 unit and the GDD provenance.
2. **Pure roster model** (new `src/MainStreetRoster.ts`): `buildCompanyRoster(state)` → ordered rows `{ memberId, staffIndex, name, roleSummary, salary, layOffCoins, layOffReputation }` plus `{ count, totalSalary }`; `companyRosterIsEmpty(state)`; `layOffReputationCost(salary)` exported for reuse/tests. No Phaser imports.
3. **Roster overlay** (`showCompanyRosterDialog()` in `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`): panel with title, one row per member (name · role/benefit · salary · `[ Lay off ]`), footer totals, `[ Close ]`, empty state; double-buffered rows rebuilt after each lay-off while the dialog stays open.
4. **Confirm step** — a small confirm dialog (or in-panel confirm state) quoting name, coin cost and reputation cost, with `[ Confirm ]` / `[ Cancel ]`, mirroring the buy-and-place premium dialog's structure.
5. **Pile hand-off** — the pile's pointer-down calls the scene's roster-open method; the pile gains no roster logic.
6. **Docs and tests** as per the acceptance criteria.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` — `letGoStaffMember()`: reputation formula becomes salary-scaled (100-unit minimum); update the doc comment.
- `src/MainStreetRoster.ts` — **new** pure model: membership filter, ordering, per-row salary/role/let-go costs, footer totals, `layOffReputationCost()`.
- `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — factor/shared staff summary line (role/benefit text) so the roster, the pile tooltip and `formatEmployedStaffSummary` cannot drift.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — `showCompanyRosterDialog()` + confirm state, modelled on `showStorylineJournalDialog()`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStaffPile.ts` — **new (from parent work)**: add the pointer-down hand-off (`onOpenRoster`); no roster logic.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererLayout.ts` / `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererContext.ts` — wire the pile's hand-off callback through the renderer context.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — `showCompanyRoster()` scene entry point (journal-button precedent).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — new i18n keys/strings for the roster's tooltip/confirm copy where the bundle pattern applies.
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — `isBusinessStaffCard()` / `computeStaffSalaryCost()` / `getSalaryScopeSkills()` (reference; no change expected).
- `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` — `letGoStaffCommand()` (reference; unchanged).
- `tests/main-street/company-roster.test.ts` — **new** unit tests: membership, ordering, totals, reputation-cost boundaries.
- `tests/main-street/company-roster.browser.test.ts` — **new** render tests: open from pile click, rows, confirm/cancel, post-lay-off refresh, empty state, hand input pass-through.
- `tests/main-street/manage-card-dialog.browser.test.ts` · `tests/main-street/staff-skill-scope-gate.test.ts` · `tests/main-street/MainStreetIntegration.test.ts` · `tests/main-street/staff-placement-removal.browser.test.ts` — update the flat −1 reputation expectations.
- `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` — D.4.2 §5: lay-off reputation cost restated in ×100 units and the salary-scaled rule.
- `docs/game/card-catalog.md` — the "lay-off costs one turn's salary plus 1 reputation" line restated.
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — Company Roster spec: entry point (pile click), rows, totals, confirm step, empty state, input pass-through.
- `src/README.md` — new roster module and the pile hand-off noted.

## Related work

- **MS-0MWBWKZ1G006IBH2** — Management company staff (Staff Pile, in progress; **blocks this item**): supplies the pile whose click opens this roster. Its ACs were amended during this intake to permit exactly one click affordance.
- **MS-0MWC952QU000HQ11** — Business staff lay-off: choose which employed member to let go (open, `discovered-from` this item): the Manage Card currently always lays off the most recently hired member; raised at the producer's request so both lay-off doors share one standard.
- **MS-0MW20VBSZ003A01O** — Staff impact (completed): the two-type staff redesign.
- **MS-0MW3LTMHT001PRDT** — Gate specialization-skill effects by staff type (completed) and **MS-0MW4MSNWR00123OZ** — Scope gate in buff aggregation (completed): the helpers that already filter management-company members.
- **MS-0MW4XULA90002OEY** — Turn summary P&L statement (completed): the nearest precedent for quoting engine-resolved per-staff costs in a UI.
- **MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE** / reputation re-tune line — the reputation rescale that makes "1 reputation" read as 100 today.
- **MS-0MUMP97LQ006PP1D** — Storyline Journal overlay (completed): the row-list overlay precedent this dialog follows.
- Docs: `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` (D.4.2 §5, D.4.4 management-company roles and salaries), `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`, `docs/game/card-catalog.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — a lay-off can collapse reputation outright.** With the new formula a €500/turn member costs 500 reputation, while Hard starts at 200 and Easy at 500 — firing a top-tier executive can end the run. *Mitigation:* the confirm step quotes the exact reputation charge before committing, and the roster shows the member's salary next to it; if a cap is wanted later, it is a one-line change to `layOffReputationCost()` plus a balance item, not a UI change.
- **Risk — drift between quoted and charged costs.** The confirm dialog could quote a salary the command does not charge (skill discounts, clamps). *Mitigation:* both the row and the confirm step read from the same pure model, which resolves salary through the engine helpers; a unit test pins the model's cost to `letGoStaffMember()`'s effect.
- **Risk — the pile's new click swallows hand input.** *Mitigation:* confine the hit area to the pile's own bounds and assert hand-card click/drag pass-through in the browser test.
- **Risk — the ×100 rescale leaks into docs inconsistently.** *Mitigation:* restate D.4.2 §5 and the card-catalog line in the same units in this item, and check the GDD-consistency test (`tests/main-street/gdd-staff-consistency.test.ts`) still passes.
- **Risk — scope creep into business-staff lay-off UX.** *Mitigation:* the Manage Card keeps its current selection behaviour; per-member selection there is MS-0MWC952QU000HQ11.
- **Assumption:** clicking the pile opens the roster from both the stack and the portrait row; the tooltip behaviour is unchanged.
- **Assumption:** the roster lists the acting seat's `state.staffCards` (the same source the pile renders), so competitive play shows that seat's own management team.
- **Assumption:** the roster is available whenever the pile is — no phase gating, matching the Manage Card's ungated lay-off today; it is suppressed in `replayMode`/headless runs.
- **Assumption:** row order is stable and deterministic (staff hire order, oldest first), so the overlay does not reshuffle under the player's pointer after a lay-off.
- **Assumption:** the ×100 reputation rescale is a documentation fix, not a data change: no `card-data.csv` reputation value is touched by this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "How is the roster opened? — A. clicking the Staff Pile (stack or portrait row), amending the parent's 'no click action' AC; B. a separate `[ Company ]` HUD button next to Journal; C. both." **Recommended:** A — the pile is already the management-company surface and the producer had deferred its click to this item.
  - Answer (producer): "A". Source: interactive reply.
  - Final: A. Pile click opens the roster; parent AC MS-0MWBWKZ1G006IBH2 amended accordingly and commented.
  - Research: parent AC bullet read verbatim from `wl show`; no other overlay entry point exists for a staff surface. GDD D.4.2 §5 ("from the company roster") supports a single roster door rather than a HUD duplicate.
- Q2: "How does letting someone go work? — A. per-row `[ Lay off ]` plus a confirm dialog quoting the cost; B. per-row `[ Lay off ]` executing immediately (Manage Card behaviour); C. select a row, then one shared button." **Recommended:** A — real money plus reputation, and the roster can be long.
  - Answer (producer): "A (make reputation loss realistic amount)". Source: interactive reply.
  - Final: A, with the reputation amount reworked per Q4/Q5.
- Q3: "What does the roster list? — A. management-company staff only with name/role/salary/let-go cost plus count and total-salary footer; B. all staff grouped with business staff read-only; C. management-company staff only, one line each, no footer." **Recommended:** A — matches GDD D.4.2 §5 and keeps business lay-off in one place.
  - Answer (producer): "A". Source: interactive reply.
  - Final: A.
- Q4: "What should the reputation loss be? — A. flat −1 as written; B. salary-scaled `max(1, ceil(salary/100))`; C. tier-scaled; D. salary-scaled but capped." **Recommended:** B — salary is already on the card and in the roster, so cost-to-cut is legible.
  - Answer (producer): "B but note that we have scaled reputation by 100 since the GDD was written. 1 should be 100". Source: interactive reply.
  - Final: B in ×100 units — `max(100, ceil(salary / 100) × 100)`: salary 0–100 → 100, 150 → 200, 250 → 300, 400 → 400, 500 → 500.
  - Research: reputation ships in ×100 units — starting reputation 200/300/500 per difficulty (`src/MainStreetDifficulty.ts`), and hand discard already deducts the card's coin `cost` from reputation (`src/MainStreetMarketHand.ts:178`), confirming 1 unit ≈ 100 display. Doc lines still quoted the pre-scale flat 1: `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` D.4.2 §5 and `docs/game/card-catalog.md:620`.
- Q5: "Which lay-offs use the new formula? — A. all lay-offs via one rule in `letGoStaffMember()`; B. management-company only." **Recommended:** A — avoids two lay-off economies differing only by which door was used.
  - Answer (producer): "A". Source: interactive reply.
  - Final: A. Engine change lives in `letGoStaffMember()`; the Manage Card inherits it and its flat −1 test expectation is updated.

# Staff Pile renderer module

## Goal

Create `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStaffPile.ts` — the module that draws the management-company staff pile: stacked card faces, count badge, portrait row, hover wiring and empty-state hiding — mirroring the `drawHandPanel()` lifecycle.

## Scope

- Create `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStaffPile.ts` as a new helper module depending only on `MainStreetRendererContext`:
  - `drawStaffPile(renderer)` — rebuilds the pile from the management-company members of `state.staffCards` on every call (destroy-then-redraw, like `drawHandPanel()`).
  - A fanned/stacked set of small card faces (oldest first, newest hire on top), each rendered with `mainStreetRenderCardSvg` at reduced size.
  - A count badge showing the number of management-company staff, drawn over the stack.
  - A small portrait row beneath the stack, one portrait per member (reusing the SVG card renderer at portrait size).
  - Hidden when the company has no management-company staff (no placeholder tile).
  - Non-interactive apart from a hover hit area confined to the pile's own bounds that shows/hides the tooltip; no `pointerdown` handlers and no lay-off control.
- Declare `drawStaffPile(): void` on `MainStreetRendererContext` (`src/scenes/MainStreetRendererContext.ts`) and delegate it from `src/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` (`drawStaffPile() { drawStaffPile(this); }`).
- Call `renderer.drawStaffPile()` from `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererLayout.ts` on the hand-refresh path, next to `renderer.drawHandPanel()`, so hires, lay-offs and `maxHandSize` changes are reflected.
- Destroy/rebuild the pile graphics per refresh so repeated refreshes do not leak game objects (same pattern as `destroyHandPanel()`).

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStaffPile.ts` — NEW: pile render module
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererContext.ts` — `drawStaffPile()` declaration
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — import + delegate
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererLayout.ts` — call on the hand-refresh path

**Headline:** The business Manage Card stops laying off whichever staff member happened to be hired last: it now lists every member employed at that business, one row each with its own `[ Move ]` and `[ Lay off ]`, and an explicit confirm step quoting the exact coins and reputation before anything is charged.

## Problem statement

The Manage Card dialog is the only door for letting business staff go, but it never asks *who*: both `[ Move staff ]` and `[ Lay off ]` act on `employedStaff[employedStaff.length - 1]` (`src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts:926,944`). A business holding two or more members therefore exposes one control per action that silently targets the newest hire, and the lay-off executes with no cost preview and no confirmation.

## Users

- **Main Street player with a staffed business (hands-on)** — employs several specialists and wants to change the team.
  - As a player, I want to see everyone employed at this business in one place, with their effect and salary, so that I can decide which specialist is worth keeping.
  - As a player, I want to press a button that belongs to the member I mean, so that I never fire the wrong specialist by accident.
  - As a player, I want the exact coins and reputation the lay-off will charge shown before I commit, so that a €500/turn executive cannot end my run unannounced.
- **Main Street player chasing business efficiency (economy-focused)** — compares each member's salary against its local effect.
  - As a player, I want each row's salary next to the member's effect, so that I can judge the cut by its savings.
- **Game designer / QA** — needs both lay-off doors to state one rule the same way.
  - As QA, I want the quoted cost to equal the charge that lands, so that a skill discount or a clamp cannot silently diverge.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Manage Card dialog renders an **employed-staff section** with exactly one row per member employed at that slot (`employedAtSlot === slotIndex`) and nothing else — management-company staff never appear. Each row shows the member's name, its role/benefit summary (from a shared formatter, not a UI-invented string) and its effective per-turn salary resolved through `computeStaffSalaryCost(getSalaryScopeSkills(member), member.ongoingCost)`.
- Rows are ordered deterministically (hire order, oldest first) and the panel sizes itself from the row count: at the maximum employment capacity of a business (`level + 1`) every row, button and the sell/close/cancel row are fully visible with no clipping or overlap; with no member employed the section renders nothing at all (today's empty-state behaviour).
- Each row carries `[ Move ]` and `[ Lay off ]` addressed to **that** member. `[ Move ]` hands the member's id to `beginStaffMove`, keeping the existing `moving-staff` choreography, the 1-action cost and the per-member destination list from `buildMoveStaffAffordance(state, member.id)` in its hover tooltip. `[ Lay off ]` opens the confirm step for that member only. Because the per-row labels are short, the section states both costs once in its own line (`Move: 1 action · Lay off: 1 turn's salary + reputation`) so neither cost is hidden behind a tooltip. No control in the dialog acts on "the most recently hired" member implicitly.
- The confirm step is an overlay quoting the member's name, one turn's salary in coins (clamped at 0) and the reputation cost from the shared `layOffReputationCost(salary)` — the single formula decided in MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA and **not re-derived here**. `[ Confirm ]` executes `letGoStaffCommand` through the undo manager (the lay-off stays undoable); `[ Cancel ]` changes nothing and returns to the member list.
- After a confirmed lay-off the dialog stays open and re-renders in place: the row disappears, the panel shrinks to fit, and once the last member leaves the staff section disappears while sell/close/cancel keep working. Rows are addressed by **member id** and resolved against `state.staffCards` at click time, so a stale row (the member is already gone, e.g. after an undo) re-renders and flashes feedback instead of acting on a shifted index.
- The activity-log entry and confirmation flash quote the charges actually applied — e.g. `Laid off <name> (−<coins> coins, −<reputation> reputation)` — replacing the hard-coded "−1 salary, −1 reputation" strings.
- Unit tests cover the pure model: membership filtering for the slot, ordering, per-row salary, coin clamp, reputation quote per row, id-addressing/staleness and the empty case; a test pins the confirm step's quoted cost to the effect of `letGoStaffMember()` (quoted == charged) including a discounted-salary member.
- Browser/render tests cover: no affordance when nobody is employed; two employed members produce two rows with two `[ Move ]` and two `[ Lay off ]` controls; the *first* row's `[ Lay off ]` lays off the *first* member (the regression this item exists for) and the *first* row's `[ Move ]` targets the first member; confirm/cancel behaviour; in-place refresh after a lay-off; the section disappearing when the last member leaves; and sell/close/cancel still working.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (`docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` D.4.2 §5, `docs/game/card-catalog.md`, `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`, `src/README.md`).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A player who has hired several specialists at one business can finally pick which one leaves — seeing each member's effect, salary and the exact lay-off price first — instead of a single button that always fires the newest hire.

## Constraints

- **Blocked by MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA.** That item lands the salary-scaled reputation rule in `letGoStaffMember()` and exports `layOffReputationCost(salary)`. This item consumes that helper and the same lay-off confirm standard; the formula is not re-litigated here.
- **One confirm step, two doors.** The confirm step is being built for the roster by its child **MS-0MWC9PCSB001MCMQ**. This item reuses the shared confirm content builder and cost helpers rather than writing a second quoting implementation; if that child lands the confirm local to the roster dialog, this item factors the shared content builder out and both call it.
- **No engine change.** No new command and no new persisted state. Membership is derived from `state.staffCards` on open and after each action; lay-off stays `letGoStaffCommand` (snapshot → undoable) and relocation stays `moveStaffCommand` (1 action).
- **Address by id, never by index.** `letGoStaffCommand(state, index)` is index-based, so a click resolves the row's member id to a current index at click time and refuses when the member is gone.
- **Pure model first.** Row building, salary/cost resolution and confirm copy live in a Phaser-free module so they are unit-testable; the overlay only draws.
- **One source of truth for figures.** Salaries come from `computeStaffSalaryCost`/`getSalaryScopeSkills`; the lay-off reputation cost from `layOffReputationCost`; the move destinations and 1-action cost from `buildMoveStaffAffordance`. No UI- or model-local arithmetic.
- **Overlay kit only.** `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton` / `dismissOverlay`, every element parented into `s.hudContainer`, depths 199/200/201, everything tracked in `s.overlayObjects`, instant appearance (reduced-motion safe), suppressed in `replayMode`/headless runs. No new art — rows are text plus kit buttons.
- **Don't touch the mechanics.** Sell, close, cancel and the move/destination flow keep their current behaviour and costs; only the staff section and its confirm step change.
- **Localisation.** New user-visible strings follow the `HUD_TOOLTIP_I18N_KEYS` / `HUD_TOOLTIP_STRINGS` English-bundle pattern where a key fits; overlay-only labels may follow the journal/undo-warning literal-string precedent.
- **UK English**, no `CHANGELOG.md` edits (managed by the release pipeline).

## Existing state

- The Manage Card dialog (`showSellConfirmation`, `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts:690-975`) is a fixed 480×410 panel: card info, sale value, a close-cost line, `[ Sell ]` / `[ Close ]` / `[ Cancel ]` at `panelY + 265`, then a single `Employed here: <names>` line (`+305`) and one `[ Move staff (1 action) ]` (`+352, centerX − 110`) plus one `[ Lay off ]` (`+352, centerX + 110`).
- Both staff handlers target the newest hire: `const moveTarget = employedStaff[employedStaff.length - 1]` (`:926`) and `const target = employedStaff[employedStaff.length - 1]` (`:944`). Neither asks for confirmation.
- Membership today: `allStaff.map((member, index) => ({ member, index })).filter(({ member }) => member.employedAtSlot === slotIndex)` (`:700-704`) — the `index` is the `state.staffCards` index `letGoStaffCommand` needs.
- `letGoStaffMember()` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:1513`) removes the member, charges one turn's effective salary clamped at 0 and a flat **1** reputation, then deregisters it from the business's `employedStaff`. `letGoStaffCommand()` (`src/MainStreetCommands.ts:903`) wraps it in a snapshot.
- `buildMoveStaffAffordance(state, staffId?)` (`src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts:613`) already accepts an explicit member id, resolves legal destinations through `canMoveStaffOnBusiness` and rejects illegal starts; today the dialog always passes the newest hire. `onMoveStaffClick(staffId)` (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts:362`) accepts any employed member's id.
- Overlay precedents: `showStorylineJournalDialog()` (`:1655`) row list with empty state and replay short-circuit; `showUndoChallengeWarningDialog()` (`:1227`) is the confirm/cancel shape; `MainStreetLoanSelectorModel` + `MainStreetLoanOverlay` is the pure-model-plus-row-list pair; `showBuyAndPlacePremiumDialog()` (`:994`) the cost-quote-then-confirm structure.
- `formatEmployedStaffSummary()` (`src/MainStreetFormatting.ts:452`) already renders per-member `• <name> (<types>) — <description>` lines for the street tooltip — the shared role/benefit text the rows should reuse rather than re-invent.
- The Manage Card only opens for an owned, non-sold, managing-phase slot (`onSellCard` → `showSellConfirmation`), and its handlers carry defensive legality guards; nothing here changes that gating.
- Tests asserting the current behaviour: `tests/main-street/manage-card-dialog.browser.test.ts` (lay-off with one member, expects −1 reputation and dialog dismissal; no-affordance empty case), plus `letGoStaffMember`-based expectations in `MainStreetApplicant.test.ts`, `staff-skill-scope-gate.test.ts`, `staff-business-type-matching.test.ts` and `MainStreetIntegration.test.ts`.

## Desired change
